ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$. Point D is on the extension line of AB, and DC is tangent to $\odot O$ at point C. If $\angle A = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line OC, \\
$\because$ DC is tangent to $\odot$O at point C, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OCD=$90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle$A=$20^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OCA=$20^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DOC=$40^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$D=$90^\circ-40^\circ=\boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is an approximately horizontal diameter, O is on AB and located near the center of the circle; B is at the intersection point on the left side of the circle, A is at the intersection point on the right side of the circle. D is located to the left of B, on the extension line of AB. C is at the lower left of the circle, the line DC passes through C and is tangent to the circle at C, and AC is also connected in the figure. Reasoning: Construct the radius OC according to the method. Because DC is the tangent to circle O at point C, the radius OC is perpendicular to the tangent DC, that is, ∠OCD = 90°. Since O is on AB, ∠OAC is the known ∠A = 20°. In triangle AOC, OA and OC are both radii, so OA = OC, triangle AOC is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠OCA = ∠OAC = 20°. Thus ∠AOC = 180° - 20° - 20° = 140°. Also because D is on the left-side extension line of AB, OD is the opposite ray of OA, so ∠DOC = 180° - ∠AOC = 180° - 140° = 40°. In right triangle OCD, ∠D = 180° - 90° - 40° = 50°.
